utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-03-68, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. Mr. Oric, are you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can indeed follow the proceedings in my own mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Oric, and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I am here together with co-counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers, and Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones I represent Mr. Naser Oric. We're joined by our legal assistant Ms. Adisa Mehic and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. And good morning to the colleagues from the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries? Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yesterday at around 5.00 p.m. We were given two previously delivered statements by our witness, Mrs. Karic, and I would like to take this opportunity to raise two issues. First of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were given by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Prosecution. First of all, we searched through the EDS very thoroughly and those statements were not there. And when we received the statements yesterday, we established that the numbers for those statements are the numbers that are simply represented by gaps in the EDS. What I'm particularly concerned about today is this: The statements I'm talking about are obviously packed with facts that come under Rule 68 and they should have been submitted to the Defence straight away for two reasons. First of all, because they cast doubts on the statements and the evidence presented by the Prosecution; and secondly, because they could benefit our client and also according to Rule 66(B) that we've been asking for from the very start, we should have been entitled to those statements because they are indispensable to the Defence for preparing the Defence case and we did not get them. However, at any rate we don't believe that this is a huge problem in relation to this witness and you'll be able to see why soon enough. But we would like to request the Prosecution to submit to us immediately all the previous statements made by our witnesses, and we believe we are entitled to make that request in line with the Rule 66(B) in order to be able to prepare our Defence case properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Before I give you the floor, Mr. Wubben, or whoever. I take it that, if I understand you well, that there are two points that you basically make what should be done in the future, but also that according to you there has been a violation by the Prosecution of the provisions of Rule 68(i). Are you insisting on measures to be taken by the Trial Chamber against the Prosecution if the Trial Chamber ultimately is satisfied that there has been such violation or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have already turned to the Trial Chamber on a number of occasions making similar objections, and it is up to you to make the decision. The decision in your hands. We are not going to start insisting on anything; it's your decision. But as to Rule 66(B), I really do believe that it is their duty and that that duty should be honoured straight away. And as to the archives of the Drina Corps, this is something that I find particularly worrying because we keep working on the searches with regard to these archives on a daily basis, day and night basically, and we've been told that it would be updated on the EDS and it hasn't been done yet. And now we've been told that it would be done by the end of September, and we keep having witnesses here who are important witnesses and in a position to testify in relation to the documents we keep unearthing. And these are important documents for the Defence, likely to clear our client, and I would really like to make this point with a great deal of insistence that we believe that all this should be available on the EDS as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I 100 per cent agree with you Madam Vidovic, there's no question about that. Who's going to respond -- who's going to respond to this, please, from the Prosecution? And this may ultimately require a written explanation if it is necessary that you go further into the matter to find out exactly why this was not disclosed earlier. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, when it comes to 6 -- the Drina Corps collection, you should be informed that there have been meetings between the Prosecution and the Defence priorly, and those meetings also end up in confirmation via correspondence to confirm our position and to update them, also clarifying that by the end of September it should be on EDS as planned. It is a big and huge operation. And it should be anyhow updated by then, but we cannot speed it up more because of all -- because of the big volume of the Drina Corps collection. Anyhow, it should be completed by the end of September, so that is within a couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Stop here for the time being. But I'm making it very clear, and of course I will consult later on with my two colleagues on this, that I would certainly not recommend to my two colleagues to allow this to happen without envisaging or leaving the possibility for remedies that might come -- become necessary for the Defence. In other words, I'm making it very clear that I will be recommending to my two colleagues that if as a result of this continued exercise regarding the Drina Corps, it's the case of the Defence calling more witnesses or bringing back some of the witnesses that they have, then I will -- I will allow it to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yes. And we respect in that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The discretion of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that would mean putting further -- even further back the completion of this case. So if there is a way -- I don't know how you -- because obviously this is not being done by you, how the process is being conducted of inputting the Drina Corps documents into the EDS. However, if it is already in electronic format and there is a way of checking at least by -- either by names or words or through what you have already, even if it is not yet in the EDS and locating any documents that might be of interest to the Defence, particularly under 66 and under 68. I mean, I won't even make a difference now at this point in time. I wouldn't wait until the whole exercise is completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Well, Your Honour, please be informed that the Drina Corps collection so far already -- well, not completely put in into the EDS is near -- is near the completion of it by the end of September, but so far is also available for the Defence to do the searches whatever they can do. And if your Trial Chamber need more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but don't give me that language please, Mr. Wubben. When we come to Rule 68, it's not a question of the Defence can search themselves and locate the documents that are exculpating. It's your obligation to disclose them as Prosecution. So that argument doesn't hold water. Don't put us in a position where we really have to be strict and inflict -- inflict sanctions on the Prosecution for having failed to comply with the requirements of Rule 68 bis. The EDS system and whatever e-court system will be in place will not diminish that little bit the responsibility that the Prosecution has of disclosing all 68 material. Am I making myself clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That has to be identified, selected, taken away from the rest, and handed over to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And that -- that disclosure has been the subject of those meetings between the Prosecution and the Defence and this is -- and that's why it's one of the services to provide them already with this collection on EDS for them to have it available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate also the difficulty in which you find yourself, Mr. Wubben. Please don't think that I -- that we do not understand that. However, please do also understand that the situation, now that the Defence case has stated, dramatically changed automatically. I mean, while you were still during the Prosecution case, you know, certain loopholes, certain mistakes. I mean, you could patch the fabric and one could -- one could go -- go forward. When you have already started the Defence and you are already more than a month and a half into it or two months into it, not to say maybe halfway through or somewhere near there, the situation changes. Yes, Madam Vidovic, for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just add one point which I believe is particularly important for the sake of the transcript. I even went as far as to suggest to the colleagues from the Prosecution to submit the CDs on the Drina Corps to us because they do have all that in an electronic version. And I said that we were willing to look for the materials we need according to Rule 68. But we received no reply to that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There I cannot intervene because the selection of the material that goes into the EDS is the prerogative of the authorities here and there is -- or there may be some material that should not be in the EDS. So I wouldn't interfere in that. However, you need to find a solution. If you don't find a solution, an agreeable solution, amongst yourselves, then I will have to impose one. Now, the other thing is the alleged violation of Rule 68 in the sense that the two documents -- I understand that two documents were not disclosed before when they were supposedly in your possession, and that when they searched the EDS the Defence found out that there were two empty slots where those documents would -- should have been. So I don't want to ask you or to insist that you respond to this now because it's an alleged violation of one of the Rules. If you want to take our time to prepare yourself properly before you answer, you can -- you can ask me for some time and I will grant you some time. But that's the position. But we need to know because alleged violations of Rule 68 we take extremely serious, also because they have been taken extremely seriously by the Appeals Chamber after the case is all over. Yes, one moment. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just clarify, Your Honours. When I talk about gaps, I don't refer to two documents only, there are gaps in documents. There may be more documents there. For example, you have a series of numbers, then a gap, and then the series continues. So perhaps it may be one, two, three, a hundred documents. There's no way of telling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Anyway, it's up to you, Mr. Wubben. If you want to reply, please do so now by all means. If you want to take some time so that you are in a position to tell us when exactly these documents came into your possession and your knowledge and when you became aware of them, then we will give you time by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I request that Ms. Joanne Richardson to respond to that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Let me say firstly that it's our position that the statements of the witness who's presently testifying we do not consider them Rule 68. But laying that aside, it was only in my preparation last night for cross-examination that it was -- it came to light that these statements had not been turned over to the Defence, and of course we took immediate action in doing so. But it is our position that the statements are not Rule 68. Perhaps certainly under Rule 66(B) they should have been disclosed to the Defence, as it could be considered material for the preparation of their case. Your Honours, the statement in our possession -- and I should say "statements," they were given by the witness in 1994 in Tuzla. There are three of them from what I can tell so far. They are all in sum and substance similar to what she has testified to today, and it is our position that there is nothing contained in them would fall under Rule 66(8) --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, 68(i). And, again, certainly under 66(B) they should have been disclosed and, once we learned they had not, we contacted the Defence about it. And at this moment we are not opposed to counsel for the Defence re-opening her examination-in-chief as she wishes to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is one other thing -- yes, do you want to comment on that, Ms. Vidovic, or should I continue myself? There is also one other thing that I remember. I mean -- yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also -- and you should have noticed that -- by now that I miss very little from the evidence while it is being given and I usually remember it almost verbatim. Yesterday in one of your examinations, Ms. Vidovic, you presented to your client [sic] that she had made several statements about the -- the events that unfortunately she had to live through. I take it, therefore, that you were au courant of statements that she had made. Were these statements you were given by the Prosecution also in your possession. If you don't want to answer, don't answer. But I think we should play our cards openly here because --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because we are take all the necessary steps --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do want to reply. Your Honour, I had two statements, one which is published in a book that I didn't get from the Prosecution and one out of those three statements, but I still did not get two other statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So the position is this: We still need to see these two statements because there is no agreement between the two parties as to whether they were 68(i) material. I have a very clear statement from Ms. Vidovic that they are, and a clear denial from -- from Ms. Richardson. We will reserve our position as regards 66. Knowing that not much harm could ensue because you're not opposing that -- for the re-opening of the examination-in-chief. But this matter of Rule 68 material needs to be considered more in depth by the Trial Chamber. So please let us also have a copy of these two documents because without having a look at them we are not in a position to know whether they are 68 bis material. And of course everything that I have said is subject to agreement between the -- between me and the other -- and the other two Judges. It's just as a start. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution will provide the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: -- Bench with all three statements in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought they were two.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, evidently they are three statements and they are all very similar in nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But we still need to see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And please make an effort. I know when it comes to this mass of documents and selecting them and then putting them in the electronic data system, it's not -- it is no simple task, but there is an ongoing stage that has reached a -- there is an ongoing case that has reached a crucial stage now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we understand that and we will make efforts to provide, especially with respect to witnesses coming up, any statements that may -- that should be turned over and have not been turned over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I -- please do try to understand -- I don't know how this case is going to finish it. It might turn up in a acquittal, it might turn up in a conviction and sentence. But whichever way it goes, I -- the problem that the Appeals Chamber encounters all the time is the -- this discovery of new documents immediately after that the case at trial stage is over. And this continued discovery goes on and doors are re-opened and closed and windows are kept ajar and it's a problem. I wouldn't -- I like to finish my cases -- if possible, have them well-baked, neither undercooked nor overcooked. And if -- please do try to understand me. I hate to give opportunities for you to appeal if there is an acquittal based on documents that you have just now discovered, and the same applies to the Defence to find out that there are documents which should have been disclosed that were not disclosed and which could have changed the -- the course of the -- of the case of the Defence. So I do appeal to you to exert the most attention, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Any further preliminaries? We will be handing down our decision on the Rule 92 bis later on today. Surely there are some minor corrections. Mr. Pittman, please, first break, so that I give it back to you. Thank you. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Karic, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, please accept my apologies for having kept you for half an hour there in the waiting room. We had a minor procedural matter that we needed to address, which has got absolutely nothing to do with your -- with your testimony but which needed some time. So we will now continue with your cross-examination. You are still testifying in virtue of the solemn declaration, to speak the truth, that you made yesterday, so you don't need to repeat it. Please make yourself comfortable, and we hope to be able to send you back home very soon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the OTP starts with their cross-examination, let me please say that yesterday I forgot to ask that the map Exhibit 750 be signed -- or rather, initialled by the witness. I believe she hasn't done it. So could she please be given D750.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for pointing that out, Ms. Vidovic. We can start with that. Ms. -- Madam Karic, look at it before you sign it and make sure that there are no changes from -- or to what you marked on it yesterday, that there are no additions or other markings. Right. Are you satisfied that it is the same map that you were looking at yesterday with your own markings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Please sign your name on the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Richardson:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Karic. My name is Joanne Richardson and I am a lawyer with the Prosecution, and this morning I will be asking you a series of questions, some of which I will be seeking clarification about your testimony from yesterday. Let me just say, first of all, that I will not be asking you questions about the rape that occurred. And the questions that I have will deal primarily with what happened in the mine and some of the events prior to that. Forgive me if I jump around and skip around a bit. I'll try to keep it in as chronological order as I can. If there's anything that I ask that you do not understand, please tell me and I will rephrase it to the best of my ability. And some of the questions that I will be asking may just require a yes or no answer and if you feel the need to explain further, you may do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm not -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the witness has understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you can -- you may proceed with your first question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'm trying to get closer to the mike. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's Karic, first I would like to ask you about your village. I believe you testified yesterday that it was a mixed village, or it was in 1992, and that there were both Muslims and Serbs in the village. And I would just like to get some clarification as to -- and forgive me, again, if you have stated this yesterday and I'm asking you to repeat certain things. Could you tell me how many Serbs were living in your village? Perhaps -- let me rephrase the question. Is it a fact that your village, Lasovac, is a purely mixed village or are there Serbs there at the time of -- in 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my village, Lasovac, we had Muslim residents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Serbs were part of the larger Sase area. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I believe you indicated on the map yesterday, Defence Exhibit 751 [sic], that there was a Serb village in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could give the map to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 750, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, 750. I believe the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It said 751.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can indicate for us where it was that you marked that the Serb village was located in the Sase area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday, the witness marked a whole number of Serb villages, so this question is confusing. The Prosecutor should clarify precisely which village, which Serb village, she had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Not a problem, Your Honour, I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is as if you were reading my mind, Ms. Vidovic, and I am actually yesterday's transcript because I myself started feeling a little bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She did actually -- first she was asked to mark a series of villages which were Sase, Odloznik -- Podloznik, Biljaca, Prisoj, Zaluzje, Voljavica, and she indicated that these were Muslim villages. Then she was asked about Gradina and she said that there was only one Serb village, Tubic, the Tubic family, Azlica, then Zala -- and Azlica, and Zalazje, Obadi, Kostanovice, Neskovici, and she indicated that they were Serb villages. And then as regards her village, as to Lasovac itself, I mean you village, you said it was a Muslim village. How many houses were there? About 30. Could you please tell what was the Serb village bordering on your village? And then she explained that it was Jaruge. And then she explained who was living in Jaruge. So to my mind yesterday it was clear. What is not clear in my mind is what is not clear in your mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, which is why I was trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So perhaps I can rephrase the question and thank you for reading out the testimony from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, I will rephrase my question. The villages that you indicated were -- that were -- that were mixed, could you tell me Serbs -- Serb families there were in those villages? Were they half and half or were they a little bit more Serb or a little bit more Muslims, if you know?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Donja Kolonija had both Serb and Muslim residents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was half/half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And if you could just show us -- just point to where that particular village is on the map, just in the interest of time. There were a number of them circled yesterday.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And which other village was mixed, other than -- other than this one?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were also the following villages: Bjelovac, Sikirici, and Pirici, all of them were mixed villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Ms. Richardson. Judge Eser, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just to get it clear. When you speak of 30 houses in Lasovac, all these 30 houses were inhabited by Muslim people or did you have Serbs among these 30 houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And this Jaruge or Jaruge, was it part of Lasovac or was it a separate hamlet? And if so, what was the population of Jaruge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jaruge was a hamlet of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Kostanovci village, and there were about 25 to 30 houses in Jaruge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And would the inhabitants have been Muslims or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson. Thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now Karic, could you tell me -- I'll like to ask you some questions about your father. I believe his name is Ehom -- Ahmo, excuse me, Karic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he served compulsory service in the JNA prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when he was 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether or not -- well, I'll rephrase the question. And your father, I believe you testified yesterday, worked in the Sase mine. Do you know how long he worked there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20-something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do? What were his duties in the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a miner. He dug in the mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know if other than just the mere digging, do you know if he was -- had a specialty?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because yesterday you testified that your father worked in the mine with Krsto Rankic. And you explained that Krsto Rankic was a mine expert and your father worked with him. Can you explain what you meant by a mine expert.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went together to work. As soon as they would come to the management office they would then part their ways and each of them would do their job. So my father knew at the time what his job was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it may have been a question of interpretation yesterday and also today I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Which is why I was asking for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I see Madam Vidovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic can probably help us here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know how this word "expert" entered the transcript. I know well that the witness said that he ignited explosives. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, it was mentioned in the sense that it did enter into the transcript yesterday for sure; I heard it. Okay. Please proceed, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It seems there is no expertise except familiarity with the job, familiarity with the job. I mean, that's how I think we ought to take it -- to understand it. And we see -- I don't know. If you think it means something different, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just seeking for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, was your father involved in -- part of his duties in working in the mine were setting explosives et cetera in the mine itself in addition to digging?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So it was only Rankic, Mr. Rankic as far as you know that was involved with explosives?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any other male relatives working in the mine as well?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire population of the Lasovac village and surrounding villages, most of them worked in the mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the -- when you say "the entire population," I take it you mean both men and women worked in the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were some women who worked in the mine because I believe you mentioned yesterday there were someone who was a typist.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They worked in the management office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So there were some women, and laying aside the actual manual work outside, digging and setting of explosives, there were some women who worked in the mine in the administrative areas?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not there was a kitchen set up for the employees of the mine? And I'm referring to prior to 1992 when everyone worked there in large numbers.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father, was he -- or other men in the village, were they hunters? Did they hunt for sport, as did many other men in different parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father did not hunt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was a very leading question. "Did your father, similar to other men in the village, hunt?" Never did this witness mention that there were any hunters in the village. However, in the meantime she had replied to this is beyond the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we have leading questions, we are in cross-examination, not examination-in-chief. So let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you are right, she had not mentioned others, but I can't stop Ms. Richardson from putting leading questions during cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the individuals who -- you said your father, just to get back to the last question, was not a hunter. Do you know if any other men in your village were hunters? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your father, do you know if he had his old JNA uniform from when he served in the military during his compulsory service?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't keep it. When he left the military, he returned the uniform that had been issued to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know if he owned a gun, a rifle, or any other type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you gave us your father's date of birth, but how old was father in 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a middle-aged man. He was born in 1953.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to talk to you a little bit about the events leading up to 1992, and specifically around the period of early part of 1992. I believe you testified that the -- the Serb women and children were leaving in large numbers. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were going?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, allegedly the families went to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it you heard this from some of the children or some of the people in the neighbouring villages?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My father said that most likely they went to see their relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why they were leaving? Were -- was anything said about the reason for them leaving?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know the reasons they had for leaving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall actually seeing them leaving, or was it a matter of the Serb children not being in school, et cetera, and other people saying that they had left?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many children were absent from school. They would leave during the night. In the morning we would see that families had left. They left their homes during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also at around the time they were leaving or probably just a little earlier in 1992, do you recall hearing shooting in the neighbouring villages, including your own?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my village there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the neighbouring villages? Did you -- do you recall hearing gunshot or fires?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard the gunfire coming from the villages of Jaruge, Andric, and Obad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were mixed or Serb villages? And forgive me if my memory isn't as sharp this morning with remembering which villages is village. But just tell me, were they mixed or purely Serb?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like to have a -- an exhibit put to the witness. Could I have a moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, P564 -- I'm sorry. Hold on a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay, it's P564. Your Honour, if I may, if the witness could be shown page 169 of the B/C/S version of the book, page 19 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, I'd like you to turn to the paragraph of that page that starts with "on 2nd March, 1992." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me just read out for the record what it says and you can follow along. "On March 2nd, 1992, a delegation from the villages of Obadi and Sase visited the municipal authorities. The villagers complained of threats and nightly shooting on the part of certain Bosniaks. Most of the complaints of the Serb villagers involved Resid Hasanovic, a member of the reserve police. The Serbs also complained that Kadir Mujic had been shooting his home-made rifle. Then there was the weekly dance of Bosniak villagers in the ethnically mixed hamlet of Donja Kolonija. The Serbs complained of shooting, petards, and noisy car sirens. Allegedly, the Serbs in the neighbouring hamlets felt disturbed and intimidated and their representatives requested that we come out and see for ourselves. The next day, we went to Sase and met with representatives of both ethnic groups in the area." I'd like to stop for a moment and I'd like to first ask you something about what is stated here in this book.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And, just for the record, it is a book authored by Besim Ibisevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My first question is: Have you read this book before?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this specific paragraph that I just read from it, some of the things that are contained. I would like to ask you about whether or not you were aware Mr. Ibisevic was part of a delegation of mixed ethnicities, meaning Muslim and Serbs, and who had been involved in speaking with local Muslims and Serbs from your area. Were you aware of that, that this -- such a council of delegation existed?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I also do not know the man you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you -- and -- so you don't know Resid Hasanovic I take it?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Resid Hasanovic. And as far as I know he came to Tuzla in the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right -- but I'm sorry. When you say you don't know the man I mentioned you mean Besim Ibisevic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just going back to the beginning of this paragraph, were you aware that Muslims -- well, particular, Kadir Mujic, is that someone that you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a relative?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cousin?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from my mother's family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is my mother's nephew, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Were you aware that he had been shooting off his rifle -- well, where does he live? Let's first establish that. What village does he live in?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He used to live in the village of Donja Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were you aware that there had been shooting going on from that village, whether it involved him or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no shooting. As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, thank you. Were you also aware of the Bosniaks holding what appeared to be some type of dance?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And also were you in talking to the other children in your age group, were you aware that the Serbs were concerned about shooting or that they were concerned about the disturbances in the villages?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to draw your attention to the latter part of that paragraph, perhaps let's start at the sentence that begins with: "They also demanded arrest." Do you see that portion? It's about nine lines from the bottom of that paragraph. It should still be on the same page, I believe. Do you see the list of names in the middle of the paragraph? One is Hamed Efendic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you go down a few lines there's a sentence which begins with: "They also demanded arrest of several Bosniaks." All right. Well, let me begin reading and perhaps you'll find it. Do you see the name Drago Sarac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the fourth column -- in the fourth line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, it's -- it's -- I'm reading just a few sentences -- as a matter of fact, I'm reading the sentence before that. So if you listen to me and follow along you'll find it. So what I'm reading precedes that. "They also demanded arrest of several Bosniaks that had been shooting their firearms, verbally abusing Serbs, or singing Ustasha songs. Bosniak representatives retorted that Serbs had also been singing their nationalistic songs, that Serbian volunteers had been passing through Sase, and that a certain Drago Sarac was setting up a paramilitary organisation. After a vigorous debate it was agreed that nightly shooting should stop, a joint patrol would monitor the situation, and that the organisers of the dance parties should apply for proper permit from the Public Security Service." All right. And I'll end there. Let me just ask you whether or not you were aware that a joint patrol had been set up.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a question with respect to the mine, and please keep that exhibit in front of you and we'll get back to it right away. Prior to April of 1992, do you recall that the individuals who worked in the mine, Bosniaks and Serbs, were having difficulties working together? Do -- were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your father mention that there were problems in the mine itself? I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall when it was that your father no longer worked in the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it -- well, let me see if perhaps throwing out a month or time period would jog your memory. Did there come a time that he was no longer in the mine? And I take it this possibly would have happened just before you fled to the woods with your family?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you don't remember if at the time your family fled to the woods that he was still working -- going to work every day in the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't working at the mine at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before I get -- perhaps you can tell us, do you know where Kadir Mujic was during 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to another portion of this exhibit and I will be referring to page 32, to page 33, and of the B/C/S that would be page 185. I will begin referring to the paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 185 is the B/C/S, I gather?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. B/C/S is 185, English is 32. And it's also in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And also I take it we don't have the complete translation of this book, do we?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's something that was promised some time back.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's in process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Karic, if you look at that page I will begin reading from the paragraph that begins: "I ordered Nurija Porobic, secretary of the National Defence Secretariat." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, in that -- keeping in that same paragraph I will begin from the sentence that reads: "According to the war schedule, Asim Redzic." Do you see his name?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, reading along with me I'll read it into the record. "According to the war schedule, Asim Redzic, Redza, from Srebrenica was in the command of the anti-sabotage platoon. He was a captain 1st class in the army reserve and used to excel in military practice at all the Territorial Defence exercise." And I should state for the record this paragraph begins with a headed date, May 6th -- excuse me, April 6th, 1992, continuing in the paragraph: "He was born in 1958 and was an employee at the head office of the Sase lead and zinc mine I invited him to my office, told him openly that we had a chance to lay our hands on 150 rifles and some ammunition." I'll stop there. Are you familiar with Asim Redzic, Redza?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware that he worked at the head office of the Sase mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the head office of the mine was located?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Gradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. My next question is whether you were aware that an anti-sabotage platoon had been established in connection with the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Turning to page 33, and if you would look at page 186. It begins with "Tuesday, 7th April, 1992." In that very first paragraph I will read from the second sentence -- from the second sentence. "Situation at Sase lead and zinc mine was becoming more and more complex. Some people proposed that the security at the mine and the police patrol in the village of Sase be stepped up." Do you recall having any knowledge of the Sase mine having patrol units?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here is around the Sase mine. However, I'm not aware of any checks or controls. I only saw the mine once I had been captured. What I mean is Gradina and the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did your father mention that the mine -- well, let me ask this: Was your father working in the mine in April of 1992, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall if he mentioned the mine having security problems?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's all the questions I have with respect to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions about the mine at this time, Your Honour, I do have a photograph that I would like to be shown to the witness and we have copies. And it's also in Sanction. Ms. Radic [sic], could you take a look -- would you take a look at the photograph that's in front of you. Do you recognise what's before you, the buildings or -- and the area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can ask her directly whether that's the Sase mine --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and then she will describe the buildings --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- if she is familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Radic [sic], this is a photograph of the Sase mine. Do you recognise it as such?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the buildings in the photograph, do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And were these how the buildings appeared in 1992 when you were held there, similar?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Let's start first with the building to the right of the photograph. There's a -- it appears to be -- in the photograph anyway it looks white and it also appears to be taller than the others. Do you know what that building is? In other words, is this an administrative building?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the -- these are the management offices for the mine in Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you held?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this building -- does this building contain more than one floor? In other words, is it a two-storey or a three-storey building?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three storeys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what floor were you held on?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was on the second and third floor?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the second and third floor?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what period of time you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to when you were held in the building in 1992, and I believe we're talking of a period of May to June.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on the first floor at the time. We were held in -- in the management offices, which were situated on the first floor of the administrative building. And when we managed to escape, we escaped on to the third floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's just clarify one thing with respect to the floor. When you say "the first floor," are you talking about the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the first floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about a floor when you go into the building and you walk up steps?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned that when you managed to escape you -- "we escaped on the third floor." Could you just provide us with some additional information. What are you referring to there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned in my statement that when an action was taking place somewhere, we were in that hall and Djokanovic, Zvonko, came into this hall and wanted to chase us out and kill us. And there was an altercation amongst the Serb soldiers, and then we managed to escape on to the third floor of the building and hide there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "we," are you referring to yourself and others?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant nine of us who had been left there, six girls and a woman with two children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the period of time you were held in this building, I believe you said it's the first floor, could you tell us -- could you describe this first floor for us so we have an idea of what it contains and perhaps tell us how big it was and also tell us how many people were held there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the relevance of this question, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there's been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where will it get us at the end?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We could have this discussion outside the presence of the witness or if you could perhaps allow me a few additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question, Ms. Radic -- Karic, excuse me. Did this -- looking at this building, did this first floor -- it appears as though there are windows. Did the first floor have windows where you were held in that area?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The windows we can see here on the facade are the windows of the staircase. And the left of the building there are other windows, and that's where this hall was. So as you get to the first floor, the hall where we were kept was to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there guards present during the entire time you were held there? And of course we're -- I'm leaving out the time that you left and you came back, but during the entire period that you were held there, both before you went to Bratunac and came back, was there always a guard there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was always a guard outside the doors to the hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let's get back to the photograph for a moment. There are some buildings to the left. Could you tell us what those buildings are, if you know? And perhaps you could tell us what they were used for during the time that you were there in 1992, if you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're referring to the building with the tall chimney I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There was a gate here and there was a guard there as well. And then there were lots of soldiers all over the place. And in one of the buildings there was a radio centre for them, radio communications centre. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that because you were able to see this out of the window or you were told?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I saw it myself through the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the kitchen that you testified to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was behind this big building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Behind the administrative -- the management or the administrative building that you just --

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is that in a separate building that we can't see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how many floors did that -- does that building have and could you tell us where in that building the kitchen was located?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it is to the right of this big white building, that's where the kitchen was, on the other side. And I don't believe it had more than one floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you go into that building with the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you go into that building and why?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Went in to peel the potatoes there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you go?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that Ms. Milovanovic was -- you saw her in the kitchen while you were held there, and that's Vojka?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see her there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost always, whenever we taken to peel the potatoes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you talk to her?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we we're not allowed to talk. They were watching us, standing to one side, and they were laughing at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They who?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the cooks who would be there at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say you were not allowed to talk, is that because someone told you not to speak to them or you just assumed you couldn't talk to them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be five or six metres away from us, and we were always taken there by guard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's get this clear. You were given strict instructions not to talk to these people, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many women did you say there were, the cooks, that is?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four, five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were all Serbs that you knew from before?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were a couple I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we're getting close to the break, unless you'd like me to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much more time do you have left?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have about a half an hour left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then I think it's fair on everyone to have a break, and we will continue afterwards, unless I see a show of hands telling me that you wish it differently. I can't see. Let's have a break. I think that's wiser. We'll have a break. We'll give the witness a little bit of a break, too. And we need to mark this document and --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- will be D754. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P573, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. P5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 73, P573. Not map, this photo. So we will have -- we will reconvene in 30 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Karic, I just have a few questions remaining for you and I'll try to be as brief as possible. I'd like to ask you a couple of questions about the circumstances under which your father took a message during the time that you were detained. You may recall your testimony yesterday that he was asked to take a message to the Muslims to surrender. Now, was he asked to take this message to your village in Lasovac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was to take the message to the woods where the refugees were, the Muslim refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he was supposed to take it to anyone in particular, any person in particular?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also your aunt was also asked to take a message, and I believe she went to Konjevic Polje. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was she asked to take this message to anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know if he actually did get to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified that your relatives ended up in Srebrenica. I just want to be clear as to which relatives you're referring to. Was it your father, your mother, as well as your brother?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My family, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your father talk to you about what happened in -- during time that he was in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't talk to him about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you haven't spoken to him since -- about what happened during 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only talked to my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the time that you were in Tuzla, were you able to communicate with your mother or father in Srebrenica in 1992 or 1993? Did they know where you were? Perhaps that's two different questions, actually. Were you able to communicate with them? And secondly, did they know that you were in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't know where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I take it that other relatives from either your village or the surrounding villages ended up in Srebrenica as well?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like the witness to be shown Prosecution Exhibit P458.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look at, let's say, starting with the English, it's on page 26. I'll be referring to the 28th of December, 1992, and it will be page 37 in the B/C/S. And I believe it's also on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, if you look at page 37, and I'm specifically referring to that -- the portion that's dated the 28 of December, 1992. Do you see that date?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I will read into the record what's stated here and then I'll ask you some questions about it. "Mirzet Mujic from Sase was brought to the Military Police station. He promised he would not behave violently and it would never happen again. "Mirzet Mujic son of Enes, born 23rd November, 1965, in Sase (Lasovac) was brought to the Military Police station on 28th December, 1992, for violent behaviour and attacking Sadeta Bajraktarevic from Sase." Now, my first question to you is do you know Mirsad Milic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the information contained here that he was the son of Enes and he was born in 1965, is that consistent with what you know about him?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you also know Sadeta Bajraktarevic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have to say that Mirsad Mujic did not live in Lasovac but rather in Donja Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And Ms. Bajraktarevic was from Sase. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She was from the village of Lasovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I don't have any other question with respect to this village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also stated with respect to what you mentioned about individuals ending up in Srebrenica. I'd like to put before you a list of names and ask you whether or not you recognise any of the names on the list. And this is a new exhibit, Your Honour, so we will be handing out copies ending ERN number 02116776 to 6777 -- well, it's one page, 6776. Thank you. Ms. Karic, if you take a look at that list and just in the interests of time I would ask you to take a look at number 5, the name, Hukic Sabit from Lasovac. Are you familiar with that individual?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is he from Lasovac as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you are familiar with some of the residents from Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know their faces but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to 18. Tahic Amir from Sase, do you see that name?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He lived in the place called Gradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Samed Hajdarevic are you familiar with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Number 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Number 23. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take number 25, Tahic Munir, are you familiar with this person?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. He also lived in Gradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have another list to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's give this --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will become Prosecution's Exhibit P574.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And we have copies of the next exhibit to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I -- with respect to this list that's placed before you, please cast your eye on number 15, Hren Rudolf, do you know that individual?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- I'm not going to read out the names, but if you look at numbers 26, 27, 28, could you tell us if you know that individual?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26 and 27, I don't know those persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know number 26 -- excuse me, 28? Do you know a Mr. -- number 28 is listed as Beriz Sehomerovic. If you don't know, that's fine, we can move on. What about the 30, 31, 32, and 33?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm just wondering because I haven't heard an answer. Do you know the persons 31, 32, 33? 30, 31? 30, 31 -- we had 26, 27, she doesn't know them. 28 I never heard her say "I don't know him,""I didn't know him." And then we have 30, 31, 32, 33.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know only the person under 33.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where do you know him from?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was my neighbour. He was also from Lasovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also know Hakija -- this name isn't on the list. Do you know a Hakija Muhic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mujic or Muhic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: M-u-j-i-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mujic. Hakija Mujic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is he also a neighbour of yours or where do you know him from?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is my neighbour and he is the brother of Bahrija Mujic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have one more to ask you about. It's not on the list, if you can tell me yes or no. Do you know an Amir Tahic -- or Tehic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is he from?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Gradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the Sabit Hukic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the village of Lasovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the Nezed Salihovic? That name isn't on the list. I'm just asking you if -- by memory, if you know that person?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is not familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And Muhamed Duganic or Dugonic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is he from?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Donja Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions with respect to this exhibit, and if we can get a P number for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become P575, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the previous document, P574, I noticed that Akif Ustic was killed twice, once on the 31st of August during an ambush and he was killed again on the 13th of October during another ambush.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think it's never a good idea to be killed at all, and twice is definitely once too many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I get your point. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He wasn't James Bond.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have a few more questions for you, Ms. Karic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have the witness shown Prosecution's Exhibit 90 at this time. If we can have page -- I'm looking at the English version, it's 30. And I think in the B/C/S it's page 29, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the portion that's before you, you were asked a series of questions about what it contained and whether or not some of the facts were accurate.
